For over four decades, Cirrus Logic has been propelled by the top engineers in mixed-signal processing. Our rockstar team thrives on solving complex challenges with innovative end-user solutions for the world's top consumer brands. Cirrus Logic is also known for its award-winning culture, which was built on a foundation of inclusion and fairness, meaningful community engagement, and delivering enjoyable employee experiences at every turn. But we couldn’t do it without our extraordinary workforce – and that’s where you come in. Join our team and help us continue to make Cirrus Logic an exceptional place to grow your career!

We are looking for a highly motivated intern to join our Product Test Engineering team, where you’ll play a key role in developing production test solutions for the high-volume manufacture of complex mixed-signal semiconductors used in cutting-edge consumer audio devices.

This internship offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of design, validation, and manufacturing, helping to ensure our products meet the highest standards of performance, reliability, and scalability. You’ll be part of a multi-functional team focused on developing innovative test methodologies and driving improvements in device testability and production efficiency.

We recruit interns year-round for Spring, Summer, and Fall 2027 opportunities. Each internship lasts 12–16 weeks and follows a full-time schedule.

This role does not offer visa sponsorship.

Responsibilities

- Assist engineers in the development and production of mixed-signal and analog ICs.

- Perform electrical bench testing and automated test equipment (ATE) analysis.

- Design and build test hardware for validation and characterization.

- Collect, analyze, and summarize performance and yield data.

- Support yield enhancement and cost reduction initiatives for ramping products.

- Contribute to New Product Introduction (NPI) efforts including matrix lot reviews, GRR, CPK analysis, and production hardware buy-off.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to manage production ramp deliverables and timelines.

Required Skills and Qualifications

- Pursuing a BS in Electrical Engineering or a related field.

- Experience with mixed-signal product engineering and IC testing.

- Proficiency with lab equipment (oscilloscopes, multimeters, waveform generators, power supplies).

- Strong verbal and written communication skills.

- Demonstrated problem-solving mindset and persistence in tackling complex challenges.

- Knowledge of yield analysis and statistical techniques (e.g., ANOVA, Regression, GRR).

- Familiarity with data analysis tools such as Spotfire, JMP, Excel, and PDF.

- Understanding of high-volume production ramps and test hardware debugging.

Preferred Skills and Qualifications

- Experience with Teradyne UFlex, Excerra, or Catalyst test systems.

- Knowledge of Linux/Unix shell scripting.

- Familiarity with IC or board-level test and failure analysis methodologies.

Cirrus Logic follows a 2+ day in-office work schedule but interns should expect to be in the office more often, up to 5 days per week, based on business needs and team preference. Interns must be based within commutable distance of the work location listed on the job posting, or willing to relocate prior to beginning their internship with Cirrus Logic.

Export control restrictions based upon applicable laws and regulations would prohibit candidates who are nationals of certain embargoed countries from working in this position without Cirrus Logic first obtaining an export license. Candidates for this role must be able to access technical data without a requirement for an export license. We are unable to sponsor or obtain export licenses for this role.

Cirrus Logic strives to select the best qualified applicant for any opening. Different approaches, ideas and points of view are both valued and respected. Employment decisions are made on the basis of job-related criteria without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, protected veteran or disabled status, genetic information, or any other classification protected by applicable law.

System Validation Intern

Location: San Jose, California, United States
Employment type: Internship

About the role

We are looking for a System Validation Intern to help validate hardware, firmware, and applications together as an integrated system. This is a hands-on opportunity to work at the intersection of software and hardware while helping improve validation coverage and accelerate deployment of next-generation data-center connectivity products.

You will collaborate with system validation, firmware, hardware, software quality, interoperability, compliance, and Product Applications teams. The right candidate is curious, execution-focused, comfortable troubleshooting from data, and eager to own a scoped validation project with guidance from experienced engineers.

What you’ll do

- Define test specifications and deliver repeatable test workflows for system-level validation.

- Execute functional, performance, stress, reliability, interoperability, regression, and end-to-end validation scenarios.

- Automate feature validation and develop scripts or utilities that improve test coverage, repeatability, and reporting.

- Investigate issues across hardware, firmware, software, and applications by reproducing failures, analyzing logs and telemetry, and documenting clear findings.

- Generate comprehensive validation reports, record test results, summarize pass/fail trends, and communicate risks, known issues, and recommended next steps.

- Support lab setup and maintain test environments, devices under test, configurations, firmware versions, and required tools.

- Track bugs through their lifecycle, including clear reproduction steps, logs, traces, screenshots, retesting, regression testing, and closure verification.

- Validate system functionality, subsystem integration, performance under load, stability, and recovery behavior.

- Support interoperability and compliance activities by sharing validation reports, known-issues lists, test results, and follow-up findings.

- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to clarify requirements, investigate complex technical challenges, and improve validation processes.

- Build dashboards, parse logs, analyze coverage and pass/fail data, and identify opportunities to make validation more efficient.

- Own a defined internship project with mentor support, provide progress updates, meet milestones, and present the project’s results and recommendations at the end of the internship.

What you bring

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.

- Coursework, research, or project experience in systems, embedded software, digital hardware, computer architecture, networking, test engineering, or hardware/software integration.

- Programming or scripting experience with Python, C, C++, Bash/Shell, or comparable languages.

- Familiarity with Linux development environments, Git version control, command-line tools, issue-tracking platforms, data analysis, and technical documentation.

- Ability to follow structured test procedures, troubleshoot from telemetry or logs, reproduce issues, and communicate findings clearly.

- Foundational understanding of computer architecture and platform components, including CPUs, GPUs, memory, storage, and PCIe devices.

- Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, attention to detail, and willingness to collaborate across engineering functions.

- Ability to ask for help when blocked, follow up, escalate appropriately, and work around obstacles while maintaining quality.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with system bring-up, hardware or firmware validation, lab testing, test automation, or device-under-test debugging.

- Familiarity with PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, I2C, I3C, or other industry protocols.

- Hands-on experience with oscilloscopes, protocol analyzers, traffic generators, power supplies, thermal-forcing systems, or other lab equipment.

- Familiarity with firmware updates, boot flows, configuration and telemetry utilities, error injection, performance counters, or recovery testing.

- Experience with interoperability, compliance, stress, reliability, or regression-testing frameworks.

- Experience building dashboards, parsing logs, analyzing pass/fail trends, or automating validation reporting.

Equal opportunity

Astera Labs is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage anyone with relevant experience to apply.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

About fab2

The fab2 team can build anything. We design all the hardware and software needed to make chips and we make the fabs, tools, and components ourselves.

We're looking for exceptional, hands-on people who can iterate to the limits of what's possible.

fab2 was founded by Sam Zeloof and Jim Keller. Sam is best known for making chips in his garage, and Jim has been a leader in the semiconductor industry for the past 40 years.

About the role

We’re hiring embedded software interns for the summer term to write the firmware and applications that run our fabs. The internship begins in May or June, with a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months. You’ll be working on an integrated engineering team building semiconductor fabrication equipment, so you’ll be exposed to some very interesting engineering problems. You’ll be bringing up high-performance tools with tight requirements in areas such as structures, optics, liquids, heat transfer, physics, and chemistry. You’ll be a good fit if you’re familiar with end-to-end system bring-up.

Our philosophy is to get things built and tested in days or weeks, not months. Because of this, a portfolio (can be your GitHub) is required to apply: show us the things you’ve actually built! For us, a good portfolio includes evidence of software engineering excellence and curiosity.

Responsibilities

- Develop real-time linux applications and microcontroller firmware in Rust for controlling semiconductor fabrication equipment

- Build backend systems for capturing and analyzing semiconductor process data

Required Experience

- Pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree or higher in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or similar field

- Proficiency in Python/C/C++

- Low level systems programming experience and good understanding of embedded systems and OS concepts (Linux/RTOS)

- Microcontroller programming experience, knowledge of microcontroller peripherals such as ADC, GPIO, PWM, SPI and I2C

Nice-to-have

- Familiarity with electronics and feedback control systems

- Proficiency in Rust

Working at fab2
We’re an early-stage hardware startup with solid funding, world-class advisors, and labs/offices in Austin, TX, Lockhart, TX, and San Francisco, CA. fab2 is committed to fair and equitable compensation. Software Interns are paid hourly, at a rate equivalent to an annualized range of $114,000–$131,000 depending on experience and education. Actual earnings vary with hours worked.

Internship Benefits:

- Housing Stipend to help with first month expenses

- Lunches daily, Dinners 3x per week, Stocked Office Kitchen with Snacks and Spindrifts

- Weekly Learning & Development opportunities

- Commuter Benefits including Parking and Late Night Uber rides from the office

- Paid Time Off inclusive of Holidays and Sick Time

- Visa Sponsorship

- Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance

- 401(k) retirement plan

- Life and Disability Insurance

We are an equal-opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

The Center of Expertise (CoE) is a global team built to solve our customers' most complex technical challenges and turn what we learn into repeatable value for the rest of the business. As our Data Analytics & Programs Intern, you'll turn raw operational and customer feedback data into insight the team can act on, and help build the content, deliverables, and program materials that make that insight usable across the business. This role is for someone who likes finding the story in the numbers and then doing something with it.

- Analyze operational and customer feedback data to surface trends, recurring themes, and the areas where customers hit the most friction

- Translate analysis into clear recommendations: what the top issues are, why they matter, and where the team should focus next

- Build reporting and dashboards that give leadership a repeatable, at-a-glance view of team performance and customer signals

- Create reusable content and deliverables — briefs, templates, enablement material, and internal documentation — that scale beyond any single customer or team

- Experience creating written or visual content for an audience — coursework, campus organizations, or a prior internship all count
